name: Wildflower seeds
description: A mix of small meadow-flower seeds. Quick to sprout in open, sunny ground.

facts.text: Mature wildflowers drop fresh seed, so one patch can become many.

name: Moss spores
description: Fine dust gathered from established moss. Settles best on damp, shaded ground.

facts.text: Moss has no seeds or flowers; it spreads by spores and fragments.

name: Fern spores
description: Spores shed from the undersides of mature fern fronds.

facts.text: Fern spores need moisture to grow into new ferns.

name: Grass seeds
description: Seed heads from ornamental grasses. Hardy and unfussy.

name: Maple samaras
description: Winged maple seeds that spin as they fall. Patience turns one into a tree.

facts.text: The paired wings of a samara slow its fall so the wind can carry it.

name: Rush cuttings
description: Young shoots of soft rush, ready to settle into wet ground at the pond's edge.

name: Twigs
description: Small fallen branches. The backbone of most natural shelters.

facts.text: Old trees and overgrown corners are the best places to find twigs.

name: Bark
description: Loose strips of bark shed by old trees. Good for roofing a shelter.

facts.text: Many beetles shelter and feed under loose bark.

name: Stones
description: Weathered garden stones, some still carrying patches of moss.

facts.text: Stone arrangements give small creatures cool, sheltered crevices.

name: Leaf litter
description: Fallen leaves and needles. Keeps a shelter damp and snug.

facts.text: Leaf litter slowly breaks down into rich soil.
